claude.notes: T11: pass as --tools. Bash can still write; D5 is enforced by the T6 integrity check (R7), not by this list.

codex.notes: T8: expressed via --sandbox scoped to the review worktree. shell can still write (R7).

agy.notes: T9: allow entries are permissions.allow grant strings (prefix-matched, e.g. command(git) covers git log) for the user-global ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json; file-read tools are auto-allowed headless and need no grant. Deny names are agy's native edit tools, defence in depth only - D5 is enforced by the T6 integrity check (R7).

grok.notes: T10: allow entries are passed as --tools (comma-joined), grok's built-in tool allowlist - unlisted tools, including the deny names, simply do not exist in the session. Headless the adapter must also pass --always-approve: grok auto-approves only built-in safe commands (git), and the first other bash call is silently cancelled - stopReason cancelled, exit 0 (verified live, grok 1.0.4). Never use partial --allow permission rules: same silent end (T3 spike). Deny names (search_replace is grok's native edit tool, 3.5) are documentation and defence in depth only - Bash stays enabled for make verify, so D5 is enforced by the T6 integrity check (R7).
